source_text: Nullo modo esse posse aliquid quod et peccatum sit et poena peccati … Et insuper iactas mea inter se dicta esse contraria; quia dixi, non quidem ut tu calumniaris, "concubitum corporum a diabolo fuisse repertum"; … sed dixi, "inoboedientiam carnis quae in carne concupiscente adversus spiritum apparet, diabolico vulnere contigisse". Et rursus, quia dixi: "Hanc legem peccati repugnantem legi mentis a Deo illatam propter ultionem, et ideo poenam esse peccati". Haec inter se asseveras esse contraria
pass_a_gloss: In no way can there be something which is both sin and punishment of sin. — And besides you boast my sayings to be contrary among themselves; because I said, not indeed as you slander, 'the lying-together of bodies to have been found out by the devil'; but I said 'the disobedience of the flesh, which appears in the flesh desiring against the spirit, to have happened by a devilish wound'. And again, because I said: 'This law of sin fighting back against the law of the mind (was) brought in by God for vengeance, and therefore to be punishment of sin'. These you assert to be contrary among themselves.
pass_b_english: There can be absolutely nothing that is both sin and punishment for sin.

Augustine reports, speaking to Julian: “And on top of this you boast that my statements contradict each other: because I said, not indeed, as you falsely charge, ‘that bodily intercourse was invented by the devil’ … but I said ‘that the disobedience of the flesh, which shows itself in the flesh that desires against the spirit, came about through the devil’s wound’; and again, because I said: ‘This law of sin, which fights against the law of the mind, was brought on by God as retribution, and is therefore a punishment of sin.’ These, you assert, contradict each other.”

choices.why: Glossary default: arbitrium is the decision-power, not a later Augustinian/Reformation free-will locus.
Julian distinguishes nuptiae from concupiscentia; do not flatten to 'lust' as a nature-sin substance.
Augustine's quoted claim that the unbaptized remain under the devil; keep the personal devil, not 'evil'.
rejected: under Satan (name not in the Latin here)

choices.choice: 2026-11-11 (claude-sumfix2-d): the old English summarised Augustine's report ('Augustine reports that Julian ...') instead of translating it. Now a translation of the Latin clause(s) that carry Julian's words or Augustine's report of them, with Augustine named as speaker where the words are his; nothing added that the Latin does not say. Omitted stretches inside a paragraph are marked with an ellipsis.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded. This row is Augustine's report; Pass A glosses only the Julian words recoverable here. This row translates Augustine's report addressed to Julian, with Augustine named as speaker; Julian's words are the quoted parts.
